newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Thousands Afghan refugees cross Turkmen border.
newsitem.headline: Thousands Afghan refugees cross Turkmen border.

text.p: At least 9,000 Afghan refugees have fled to Turkmenistan from war-torn areas of northern Afghanistan in the last week, a senior aid official said on Sunday.
"The figure is accurate," Bob McKerrow, the head of the Almaty-based regional mission of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, told Reuters.
He said the refugees were concentrated in three locations in the desert area on the Afghan-Turkmen border.

Former Soviet republics neighbouring Afghanistan have voiced concern that the fighting between Islamic Taleban militia and local warlords for control over northern Afghanistan would trigger an exodus of civilians, but no major influx of refugees had been reported so far.
The federation's Almaty office said in a statement on Sunday that the refugees had fled from fighting in the town of Mari Chak of the Afghan side of the Murgab River which separates the two states.
"Turkmen authorities allowed the refugees into a no man's land on the Turkmen side of the border on Monday last week to escape serious fighting on the Afghan side," the statement said.
Turkmen officials could not be immediately reached for comments.
